note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

signal_glossary.tvl_surge: On-chain TVL jumped ≥25% in 7d from a small base — real capital arriving, not just token price.

pre_winner_lookalikes.method: validated winner-DNA coil screen (deep-below-high + oversold + at-30d-low [all validated, hold OOS] + below-ATH/high-vol/mid-float/small-cap); primed-but-not-yet-moved. NECESSARY-not-sufficient setup — needs an event trigger.
pre_winner_lookalikes.how_to_use: Beaten-down coils matching the data-validated winner DNA. SETUPS, not buys: most never move. Edge comes ONLY from confluence — a lookalike that is also trending / in a heating narrative / has a near catalyst / has fresh dev-gov.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

This release fixes critical flaws in nearcore that could cause node crash/DoS.
Upgrade as soon as possible to avoid node downtime.

## Protocol
#### Sui Protocol Version in this release: `142`

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28590: Protocol version 141 counts accumulator writes, ID-only object changes and unchanged consensus objects toward the transaction effects size limit, and limits a transaction to 1024 accumulator events. The changes previously planned for version 141 move to version 142.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28230: `groth16::verify_groth16_proof` now aborts with `EInvalidVerifyingKey` when the prepared verifying key does not contain exactly one more `vk_gamma_abc` element than the number of public inputs, instead of returning `false`.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28241: Adds `sui::clock::borrow(): &Clock` to the Sui framework. It returns the Clock without it being a transaction input, at the same timestamp as a Clock passed into the same transaction, so functions can read the time without callers passing a Clock down. Available from protocol version 141 with the framework upgrade.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28418: Adds `sui::derived_object::release`.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28460: `secp256r1_ecrecover` now aborts with `EFailToRecoverPubKey` on a signature whose recovered x-coordinate r + n overflows, instead of returning a key that does not verify it. Honest signers never produce such a signature.

> We recommend that all `atlantic-2` validators and node operators update to `v6.8.0-rc3`. The update is required for RPC nodes. There is no governance proposal and no coordinated chain halt.

`v6.8.0-rc3` is a release candidate on top of `v6.8.0-rc2`. It makes wide `eth_getLogs` queries cheaper for RPC nodes and stops them early when the client cancels ([#4744](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/pull/4744), [#4790](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/pull/4790), [#4791](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/pull/4791), [#4799](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/pull/4799), [#4802](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/pull/4802)). It also includes the `v6.7.4` trace fix, so `debug_trace*` loads a past block's full validator set ([#4811](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/pull/4811)).

Wide log queries (over 100 blocks) share a node-wide limit of 30 queries per second. You can now change it with `large_log_query_rps` under `[evm]` in `app.toml`. Set it to `0` to turn the limit off. If the key is missing, the limit stays at 30 ([#4800](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/pull/4800)).

3. Replace the `seid` binary with `v6.8.0-rc3`. If you use Cosmovisor, replace the binary in `upgrades/v6.8/bin/`.
4. Start the node.
5. Make sure that `seid version` shows `v6.8.0-rc3` and that the node syncs new …[truncated]

v2.11.0 is a hardfork, security and stability release on top of `v2.10.3`. It's the public release of `v2.11.0-priv`, which validators and major RPC providers already run.

## Uburu hardfork

Already active on both networks:

| Network | Fork block |
| --- | --- |
| Amoy | `51978200` |
| Mainnet | `96787900` |

Uburu updates the StateReceiver genesis contract (`0x…1001`) at the fork block. It changes how state syncs are executed and recorded.

- Operators on `v2.11.0-priv`: same code, switch to `v2.11.0` at your next maintenance window.
- Nodes still on `v2.10.3` or older stopped following the chain at the fork block. Upgrade immediately.

## Highlights

- **Consensus and state sync**: state-sync records are fetched from Heimdall one page at a time, as the per-block budget admits them. A failed fetch now fails the block, where before it committed it without state syncs. Span lookups by block number follow Heimdall's rule (the highest-id span containing the block). Locally sealed blocks are checked against whitelisted milestones before they're written. Header verification bounds block numbers and base fees on every import path.
- **Execution**: BlockSTM bounds speculative work per block and falls back to serial execution when the bound is hit.
- **Stateless / witnesses**: witness messages are bounded on receive, and witness-caused import failures are charged to the peer that served the witness.
- **State serving**: snap range serving and state iterators no longer read …[truncated]

## Overview

> [!NOTE]
> All op-reth operators should upgrade to this release. It contains a fix for the interop transaction pool's `endpoint.up` metric.

## Other changes

### Metrics

- The interop transaction pool's per-endpoint `optimism_transaction_pool.interop.endpoint.up` gauge no longer drops to 0 when an interop filter answers `-321100` (out of scope). A healthy filter gives that answer for any message newer than what it has ingested or cross-validated, so the gauge dipped during normal operation. `-321100` still counts as `unavailable` in `endpoint.verdicts` and still does not count toward quorum. An alert on `endpoint.up` should be paired with per-endpoint `verdicts` rates or the filter's `op_interop_filter_default_ingestion_lag_seconds`, since `endpoint.up` now keeps its last value for a filter that stalls without raising an error (#23951)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/compare/op-reth/v2.8.1...op-reth/v2.8.2

**🚢 Docker Image:**

- https://us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v2.8.2

This release is available as a Docker Image on Docker Hub at `offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.12.2-5f02f3f`
This Docker image specifies default flags in its entrypoint which should be replicated if you're overriding the entrypoint: `/usr/local/bin/nitro --validation.wasm.allowed-wasm-module-roots /home/user/nitro-legacy/machines,/home/user/target/machines`

If you're running a validator without a split validation server (this will be true of most validators), you should instead use the image offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.12.2-5f02f3f-validator which has the extra script `/usr/local/bin/split-val-entry.sh` as the entrypoint.

### base-reth-node
- **Reth V2 Snapshots** To benefit from V2, you must both update to 1.2.0 and update your database to use v2 storage. You can do this via:
  * **Recommended:** Download a new snapshot `base-reth-node download`. See the [docs](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/node-operators/snapshots) for more information.
  * Migrate your existing V1 data `base-reth-node db migrate-v2`. Note: `migrate-v2` is expected to take **much** longer than `download`. Non-archival nodes are not supported for this command.

governance.title: [Constitutional] AIP: Approve Release of Frozen ETH and ARB
governance.body:
**Authors:** Binance  
**Proposal Type:** Constitutional AIP

# Abstract

This proposal asks the ArbitrumDAO to approve the release of the 8,425.997 ETH and 74,559,805.2 ARB currently immobilized on Arbitrum One. The funds were frozen by the Arbitrum Security Council as part of a wider ecosystem effort to halt the theft of funds due to the exploit of Binance’s hot wallet. The released funds will be returned to Binance, from whose wallet they were stolen, and applied as described under “Use of Funds” to help make affected Binance users whole.

# Motivation

On 29th October 2026, the Arbitrum Security Council froze 8,425.997 ETH and 74,559,805.2 ARB held by the exploiter on Arbitrum One and moved the funds to 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000DA0. This action by the Security Council, which was acting in a true security emergency situation, was part of a wider ecosystem effort that has [frozen over $3bn](https://x.com/binance/status/2115993361517891592 "https://x.com/binance/status/2115993361517891592").

While Binance is committed to covering all losses from the SAFU Fund and the company’s treasury, we want to take this opportunity to work with Arbitrum Governance and recover …[truncated]
